title: Fats and Lipids — Structure, Classification and Functions
shortDescription: Triglycerides, fatty acids, rancidity and the numbers (iodine, saponification, peroxide) that characterise oils.
genZNote: Fat isn't the villain, the plot twist is WHICH fat and how oxidised it got. Iodine value, peroxide value — learn the receipts.

sections.heading: Structure and Classification
bullets: Triglyceride = glycerol + 3 fatty acids (ester bonds). Others: phospholipids (lecithin), sterols (cholesterol), waxes, glycolipids.

Fatty acids: saturated (no double bond), monounsaturated (oleic), polyunsaturated (linoleic ω-6, α-linolenic ω-3); essential fatty acids are linoleic and α-linolenic acid. EPA/DHA come from fish/algae.
Trans fats: formed in partial hydrogenation; raise LDL and lower HDL; limited by FSSAI.
Melting behaviour: more unsaturation and shorter chains → lower melting point; ghee/butter contain short-chain acids.

Volatile water-soluble fatty acids — butter fat is high

sections.heading: Functions, Rancidity and Processing
bullets: Energy 9 kcal/g; carrier of vitamins A, D, E, K; essential fatty acids; satiety; cell membranes; insulation.

Hydrolytic rancidity (lipase, moisture) → free fatty acids; oxidative rancidity (O2, light, metals) → peroxides → aldehydes and ketones; prevent using antioxidants (tocopherol, BHA, BHT, TBHQ), low temperature and opaque packaging.
Refining: degumming, neutralisation, bleaching, deodorisation; hydrogenation converts liquid oil to semi-solid fat (vanaspati).
Smoke point: temperature at which oil visibly smokes; frying oil limit TPC (total polar compounds) 25% in India.
Intake advice (Indian guidelines): fat roughly 20–30% of energy with limited saturated and trans fats.

quickRevision.oneLineDefinition: Lipids are water-insoluble biomolecules — mainly triglycerides — that supply concentrated energy, essential fatty acids and fat-soluble vitamins.

commonTraps: Do not say saponification value measures unsaturation.
mustRemember: Iodine value ↔ unsaturation; saponification value ↔ chain length.
